stem: A customer at a Massachusetts pharmacy counter asks to buy 5 grams of pseudoephedrine base today. He mentions that he bought 5 grams elsewhere eleven days ago. Which statements about the federal quantity limits are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A regulated seller may sell him up to 7.5 grams in a single calendar day.
The pharmacy is the party federally restricted to 3.6 grams per purchaser per day.
Today's sale would exceed the 3.6 gram daily seller restriction.
Buying a further 5 grams within the 30-day window would put the purchaser over the 9 gram limit.
The 9 gram limit applies to sellers rather than to purchasers.

explanation.core_reasoning: The two limits bind different parties under different instruments. 21 CFR 1314.20(a) restricts a regulated seller from selling any purchaser more than 3.6 grams of pseudoephedrine base in a single calendar day, so a 5 gram sale is over the seller's daily ceiling. 21 U.S.C. 844(a) makes it unlawful for any person to purchase at retail more than 9 grams during a 30-day period, so a purchaser who already bought 5 grams eleven days ago would cross that prohibition. The 7.5 gram figure in 21 CFR 1314.20(b) is a 30-day limit and applies to mobile retail vendors.

choice_analysis.A: 7.5 grams is a 30-day figure for mobile retail vendors, not a daily allowance.
choice_analysis.B: The daily restriction does bind the seller, but this option omits that the sale here exceeds it.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: 5 grams in one day is above the 3.6 gram daily seller restriction.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: 5 plus 5 grams inside 30 days crosses the 9 gram retail purchase prohibition.
choice_analysis.E: The 9 gram limit is framed as a prohibition on the person purchasing at retail.

related_facts: Massachusetts requirements apply alongside the federal limits rather than instead of them
explanation.mpje_trap: Three real figures are in play and each belongs to a different party or period, so a candidate who remembers the numbers but not who they bind can pick any of them.

reasoning_steps: Separate the seller's daily restriction from the purchaser's 30-day prohibition
Apply the daily figure to today's proposed sale
Add the earlier purchase to test the 30-day purchase prohibition
